title: sticky-span-annotations-and-compare-handoff
content:
Context:
This doc collects design notes, interaction sketches, and grooming items for two related features: (A) span-level sticky annotations (persisting comments/metadata on spans and time ranges) and (B) a compact multi-trace compare overlay that lets engineers line up equivalent spans across traces for fast regression triage. Goal is to scope an initial MVP that is high-value for on-call/debugging workflows and groom a backlog for phased delivery.

High-level user needs observed:
- Annotate a suspected problematic span during live incident triage and have that note persist across sessions and be linkable in Slack / Jira.
- Quickly compare two traces from different deploys and highlight matching spans by operation name and timing to spot regressions.
- Narrow the view to a time window and share a permalink that reproduces the same zoom + selected spans.
- Avoid performance regressions when viewing long traces (10k spans).

Design principles / constraints:
- Lightweight: annotation flow must be 1-2 clicks from the trace viewer. No modal hell.
- Non-destructive: annotations are metadata, not edits to trace data.
- Scoped permissions: annotations should support team visibility / private vs public flags.
- Portable: saved annotation links can open the Console with the same zoom and active selection.

Interaction sketches (textual sketches for handoff):
1) Hover & quick note
   - Hover over a span: show a compact tooltip with span name, duration, and a small "+note" icon.
   - Click "+note" opens an inline composer anchored to the span (max 2 lines by default).
   - Composer actions: Save (public/private toggle), Assign (optional dropdown to teammates), Tag (free-text).

2) Pin / Sticky annotation
   - After saving, a small sticky icon appears on the left of the span bar (color-coded by tag/severity). Hovering shows note preview; clicking opens side-panel with full thread.
   - Sticky is persisted to metadata store and has id: ann-<hex>. Visible in trace list as "Has notes" indicator.

3) Multi-select annotations (grouping)
   - Shift+click to multi-select spans across the same trace. Selected spans get a subtle highlight and a group annotation option appears in the floating bar: "Annotate selected (group)".
   - Group annotations attach to a logical group with a time-range anchor and a generated name (editable).

4) Timeline share / permalink
   - Permalink captures: trace id(s), zoom time window, selected span ids, and active compare set.
   - UI: share button top-right -> "Copy link" / "Open in new tab" / "Create Jira" (prepopulates summary + permalink).

5) Compare overlay (MVP)
   - Trigger: select 2 traces from trace list -> click "Compare" -> overlay mode opens over the primary trace.
   - Overlay maps spans by operation name and approximate time offset. Matching spans are connected with thin lines; mismatches greyed.
   - Clicking a connected line zooms both traces to the matched span pair in split view.
   - Persistent annotations show on both traces if they reference the same span name or explicit span id mapping.

6) Keyboard & accessibility
   - Keybindings (configurable): n/p for next/prev span, s to star/pin annotation, / to focus quick filter input.
   - Ensure screen-reader labels on annotations, ability to open side-panel via keyboard.

Wireframe notes for engineering handoff:
- No heavy DOM overlays per-span for 10k spans; we should virtualize span rows and only mount annotation icons within viewport.
- Use SVG layer for connectors in compare overlay; draw sparse bezier lines; debounce reflows during zoom.
- Annotation store: small document DB (annotations keyed by trace id, span id, user, visibility). Keep payload small (text + tags + references).
- Permalink format: /traces/{traceId}?start=...&end=...&selected=ann-123,span-456&compare=traceBId. Consider shortening with an alias service for long URLs.

Backlog (Rough grooming, prioritized):
- R1 (MVP)
  - RINF-2210: Inline composer + save annotation (public/private) (2 wks)
  - RINF-2211: Sticky icon + hover preview + side-panel thread (1 wk)
  - RINF-2212: Share permalink capturing zoom + selection (1 wk)
- R2
  - RINF-2234: Shift+multi-select + group annotation (1.5 wks)
  - RINF-2240: Basic compare overlay (2 wks)
- R3 (polish)
  - RINF-2251: Assign to Jira integration + create ticket flow (3 days)
  - RINF-2255: Team visibility + annotation access controls (1 wk)
  - RINF-2260: Annotation search & filters (by tag/user/time) (1 wk)

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Can add a note to a span that is visible to the user later (persistence across sessions).
- Notes surface as a small sticky icon in the trace viewer and open a side panel thread.
- Share link reproduces zoom + selected span(s) in a fresh browser tab.
- Viewing a 10k-span trace remains interactive: annotation icons are only mounted for visible span rows (no >100ms frame drops observed on staging).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do annotations belong in our primary event-store or a separate annotations service? Tradeoff: cross-account joins vs consistent backups. (Engineering prefers separate small doc store).
- Naming: "Sticky" vs "Pin" vs "Flag" — product preference? (Design leans to "Pin" for verbs; ops folks like "Flag").
- Default visibility: Should saved notes be private by default or public to org? Default private reduces leakage risk.
- Export format: should annotations be exportable with trace JSON for external forensic workflows? (Desired by SRE teams).

Edge cases & mitigations:
- Trace TTL / deleted traces: if a trace is deleted, annotations remain but show as orphaned with link to archived snapshot.
- Span id collisions across models/runtimes: annotations should store trace id + span id canonical pair; allow fuzzy mappings for compare.
- Large group annotations: impose a 5k-char limit and auto-collapse long threads in UI.

Handoff checklist for design -> eng:
- Deliver a small clickable prototype (Figma frames) for inline composer + pinned state (Lina) — due EOW.
- Provide SVG spec for connector lines and perf notes (Marco).
- Backend: prototype annotations table schema + API endpoints for create/read/query (Priya).
- QA: perf budget tests for 5k and 10k span traces; regression checklist for keyboard interactions (Ethan).

Notes to self / grooming meeting points:
- Demo a quick flow: annotate a slow DB span, copy permalink, create Jira -> show to oncall team.
- Ask SRE in grooming: what fields are mandatory for a Jira create? (stack trace + trace permalink + timestamp).
- Consider later: an ML suggestion to auto-tag spans with likely cause (db/timeout/retry) based on pattern matching.

Attachments & mocks referenced:
- figma: /file/StickyPin-Composer (prototype frame v2)
- slack thread: #trace-grooming 2025-07-11 (early feedback)

Next steps:
- Finalize wording for composer (short + clear): placeholder = "Add note about this span (optional: @assign, #tag)"
- Wireframe finalization for engineering handoff by 2025-07-18.
- Create Jira epic RINF-2200 and link all tickets above.

---
If reviewers: please call out any privacy/security concerns (especially around default visibility) and any perf objections to inline icons in large traces.
